reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs with no comment, which is the expected output for a compliant finding.
Party alignment is correct: Corio is the licensee/customer we represent and Commerce One is the licensor; the rule only bites where the Customer pays liquidated damages.

The cited clauses support compliance — §11.1 allows termination at end of term on 30 days' notice with no early-termination or minimum fee, §11.2 provides breach termination with no pre-agreed damages, §11.3 continues only ordinary payment/maintenance obligations, and §4.1/Exhibit B impose only ordinary license fees, so the clause set sits at the preferred position (no Customer-payable LD or penalty).
The rationale correctly treats the §4.4 audit cost-reimbursement as a cost-shifting mechanic rather than a penalty, and no deterministic check flags contradict the analysis.
